input_angle
label: Turn the input
description: Drag it: the input shaft turns and every gear follows by its tooth ratio, meshing at every angle. The range is one full turn of the output.

name: ratio_wanted
label: Overall ratio
description: Input turns per output turn. The teeth are whole numbers, so the ratio you get (an output) is within a few tenths of a percent of it.

name: input_speed
label: Input speed (rpm)
description: Speed of the motor or the driving shaft, in revolutions per minute: 1450 for a 4-pole motor, 960 for a 6-pole one at 50 Hz.

name: driven_machine
label: Driven machine
description: How hard the driven machine runs, with an electric motor driving: sets the application factor KA (ISO 6336-1) on the torque the gears and shafts are sized for.

name: gear_steel
label: Gear steel
description: Steel of the gears and pinion shafts; the teeth are sized to stay within a third of its yield strength (Lewis).

name: input_power
label: Power (kW)
description: Power the reducer carries, in kW. The modules, face widths, shafts and bearings follow from it; the upper limit (30 kW at most) keeps the gears within an 8 mm module in stage 1 and 10 mm in stage 2 by strength, and the output shaft within 95 mm.

name: cast_wall
label: Cast wall thickness
description: Wall of the grey iron housing: about 10 mm for a hand-moulded casting (VDG K 200). The rounds, flange, bosses and bolts follow it; the thickest allowed grows with the reducer, 10 mm on the smallest, 16 mm from an 80 mm output bearing bore.

name: show
label: Show
choices: Machined parts: shafts, wheels, spacers, covers
description: Open shows the gears in the lower half; Closed the reducer as it runs. Castings and Machined parts leave only those bodies, so that exporting the model as STEP gives the pattern maker or the machine shop just their parts.

title: Two-stage gear reducer
author: 3DCraft Jigs
description: A two-stage spur gear reducer in a split cast iron housing, sized from the ratio, speed, power and driven machine you give: involute teeth to the ISO 53 rack, modules from ISO 54 by the Lewis formula, shafts from the torque, 62-series bearings for 20 000 h, and a slider that turns every gear. A first sizing: have it checked to ISO 6336 before you make it. To export: set Show to Castings and export the model as STEP for the pattern maker, or to Machined parts and export STEP for the machine shop; Closed exports the whole reducer.
